title: Instructional Designer
description:
Position Overview

The Instructional Designer (ID) is an integral team member in
developing online courses and digital assets for Butler University.
The ID is part of the Digital Learning Team and the broader Online
Education and Educational Technology (OOET) team at Butler. OEET
partners with colleges, programs, and departments to create quality
online education and support learning through innovative
technology.

More specifically, the ID is crucial in creating engaging and
meaningful learning experiences for online students. This position
partners with subject matter experts (SMEs) to utilize
instructional design principles and educational technologies to
design, build, and evaluate effective, engaging, and accessible
online learning materials that meet the diverse needs of students
while maintaining quality and online compliance standards.

The OEET team allows for a remote schedule. We support our
employees in doing their best work with technology through remote
collaboration and intentional strategies to foster a positive work
culture. Butler University hires candidates with approved state
residency according to state authorization agreements with a
preference for Indiana.

To be considered for the position applicants must submit a
cover letter with their application materials.

Responsibilities

Develop collaborative partnerships with Subject Matter Experts
(SMEs) who serve as course authors, to create engaging,
high-quality, and accessible online courses.

Collaborate with SMEs to create courses that align with
instructional design standards, pedagogical and evidence-based best
practices, accessibility requirements, and institutional and
program learning outcomes.

Create SME-developed instructional content using interactive
activities, simulations, and assessments within the Learning
Management System (LMS) that align with best practices in online
education to enhance student engagement and facilitate knowledge
retention.

Analyze data to inform the design of effective learner-centered
experiences and drive continuous improvement efforts of learning
experiences.

Ensure all learning materials and course content comply with
Section 508 accessibility standards and Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines (WCAG), making courses fully accessible.

Evaluate, recommend, and effectively integrate appropriate
educational technologies to support the student learning
experience, align with outcomes, and maintain accessibility
standards.

Oversee and coordinate multiple projects concurrently with
various stakeholders, ensuring the timely and efficient delivery of
high-quality course content.

Establish and maintain positive relationships with team members
and stakeholders, understanding their strengths and skill sets,
communication styles, and motivation, to effectively drive
results.

Facilitate faculty development in instructional design
principles, pedagogical and evidence-based practices, and
educational technologies related to online learning.

Stay current with emerging trends in instructional/learning
design, educational technology, online education, and higher
education.


Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree

Experience in learning experience design, instructional design,
e-learning development, training, or related field.

Experience designing and developing engaging, innovative, and
aligned online instructional material and assessments.

Ability to collaborate with faculty from a wide range of
subject matter areas and understand unique program needs to
recommend best practices for course design.

Knowledge of adult learning theories, instructional design
models, multimedia learning principles, universal design for
learning, accessibility standards, and copyright laws.

Proficiency with course authoring/production tools, learning
management systems, Google Suite, Microsoft Suite, and video
conferencing.

Ability to take initiative, prioritize work, and manage
multiple projects simultaneously to achieve desired results.

Ability and willingness to work independently and in a team
environment, including physical or virtual environments with a
passion for supporting and serving as an advocate of diversity,
equity, and inclusion.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability
to clearly explain instructional design concepts to non-technical
stakeholders.


Preferred Qualifications

Experience in office suite, with an emphasis on excel.

Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational
Technology, or related field.

2+ years of experience designing online learning experiences,
specifically in higher education settings.

Proficiency with Canvas; e-learning innovative authoring tools
such as Articulate, H5P, or similar; HTML, and DesignPLUS.

Quality Matters (QM) certification or experience applying QM
Standards.

Certification or demonstrated experience in project management
(e.g., PMP, Agile, or related training).

About Us

Butler University is a private, nationally recognized comprehensive
university encompassing seven colleges: Arts, Business,
Communication, Education, Liberal Arts & Sciences, Pharmacy
& Health Sciences and Founder's College. Approximately 4,500
undergraduate and 1,000 graduate and doctoral students are enrolled
at Butler, representing 46 states and 24 countries.

Join us at the crossroads of tradition & transformation. A
career at Butler University offers more than just a job—it’s an
opportunity to join a dedicated, innovative, and supportive
community grounded in equity, academic excellence, and meaningful
impact. Aligned with Boldly Butler, our strategic plan, faculty and
staff play a vital role in delivering transformational learning
experiences, enriching our campus and community, and ensuring a
thriving Butler for generations to come.

Butler University is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome
applications from all individuals, regardless of age, sex, race,
religion, color, disability, protected veteran status, national
origin, or any other legally protected category.
